title: EOC Command Desk: Cannery, Hospital Oxygen and Spruce Hill, 12:05

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EOC Command Desk, Kellerton (Line 1 + Radio Patch)

callee.name: Director Gwen Halvorsen
callee.label: EOC Command Desk, Marlow County EOC

transcript.speaker: EOC Command
transcript.text: EOC Command, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Okafor (Pacific Reach Seafoods)
transcript.text: This is Tom Okafor, plant manager at Pacific Reach. I've got all 120 of my workers up on the hill, everybody's accounted for. But I've got about two million dollars of product sitting in the blast freezers with no power, and the ammonia system needs somebody to close the king valve before something lets go.

transcript.speaker: Okafor (Pacific Reach Seafoods)
transcript.text: Give me thirty minutes and four people down on the Alder River flats. The water's way out right now. I can see the mud from here. This is the window. Can I send them or not?

transcript.speaker: EOC Command
transcript.text: EOC Command. Line 2, Doctor, go ahead.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Naomi Fitch (Hospital CMO, 541-555-0142)
transcript.text: This is Dr. Naomi Fitch at the Station 3 apron. Two of my patients are hypothermic, and one is on oxygen with about forty minutes left in the tank. Our oxygen stock is in the hospital basement.

transcript.speaker: Dr. Naomi Fitch (Hospital CMO, 541-555-0142)
transcript.text: I have two staff who know exactly where the cylinders and the warming blankets are. In and out, fifteen minutes. Can I send them back in?

transcript.speaker: EOC Command
transcript.text: Copy, Doctor. Stand by. Engine 31, EOC Command, go ahead with your traffic.

transcript.speaker: Engine 31 (relaying Spruce Hill volunteer lead Marcy L.)
transcript.text: EOC, Engine 31 on Spruce Hill, relaying for the volunteer lead, Marcy. About three thousand eight hundred people up here. Everybody's soaked. One man collapsed, and we're working him now.

transcript.speaker: Engine 31 (relaying Spruce Hill volunteer lead Marcy L.)
transcript.text: The Cedar Court wheelchair residents are sitting out in the rain on the shoulder. There's a crowd by the Hemlock end chanting to go back down. Her words: if you don't give them something, they're going to walk.

transcript.speaker: Engine 31 (relaying Spruce Hill volunteer lead Marcy L.)
transcript.text: EOC, what do I tell them? Are they staying up here, and where do the people who need care go?

transcript.speaker: Okafor (Pacific Reach Seafoods)
transcript.text: EOC, Okafor again on Line 1. My guys are standing at the top of the road with their boots on. I need a yes or no.

instructorNote: This is a decision point. Command has to choose between holding the XL and XXL evacuation and allowing a limited early return for the ammonia king valve or the hospital oxygen while larger waves are still coming in. Holding is defensible when it cites the STWE 8 return criteria (NTWC cancellation and the Port Alder gauge below 0.3 m for two hours). A bounded re-entry is defensible only if Command sets its limits first (who, how long, a spotter and radio, a retreat trigger) and says what it is trading. The local instruction should use the same zone names as the warning. Field should move the apron patients, Cedar Court residents and the collapsed man up to Kellerton or the Marlow Coast High School shelter, and should look for oxygen somewhere else, such as fire or EMS stock or another source outside the zone.
